title: Intervene or Trust CLIP? Competence-Gated Adaptation for Source-Free Cross-Domain Few-Shot Learning
abstract: arXiv:2611.28104v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Source-free cross-domain few-shot learning (SF-CDFSL) adapts a pre-trained vision-language model such as CLIP to a distant target domain from a handful of labeled images, without access to source data. Recent methods improve the fine-tuning of CLIP with token-level interventions and apply them in the same way to every target domain. In this paper, we find that whether an intervention helps depends on how well frozen CLIP already recognizes the target domain: in 5-way 1-shot tasks, intervening improves accuracy by 0.72 points where frozen CLIP misclassifies most support images, but lowers it by 1.31 points where frozen CLIP already classifies them well, and the support set of a single episode suffices to tell the two cases apart; a bias-variance analysis explains both. translated_title: 是干预还是信任CLIP？面向无源跨域少样本学习的能力门控自适应方法
translated_abstract: 无源跨域少样本学习（SF-CDFSL）旨在在不访问源数据的情况下，仅利用少量标注图像将预训练的视觉-语言模型（如CLIP）适配到差异较大的目标域。近期方法通过token级干预来改进CLIP的微调，并以相同方式将干预应用于每个目标域。本文发现，干预是否有帮助取决于冻结的CLIP本身对目标域的识别能力：在5-way 1-shot任务中，当冻结的CLIP错误分类大多数支持图像时，干预可将准确率提升0.72个百分点；而当冻结的CLIP已能较好分类支持图像时，干预反而会使准确率下降1.31个百分点；并且单个episode的支持集就足以区分这两种情况，偏差-方差分析对两种现象均给出了解释。基于这一发现，我们提出了能力门控自适应方法（Competence-Gated Adaptation, CoGA），该方法在标注支持集上测量冻结CLIP的准确率与边际，并在训练之前决定是否进行干预。
tldr: 该论文发现token级干预只在冻结CLIP对目标域识别能力较弱时有效，据此提出能力门控自适应方法CoGA，通过在支持集上评估CLIP的准确率与边际来在训练前决定是否干预，从而提升无源跨域少样本学习的性能与稳定性。
en_tdlr: This paper finds that token-level interventions on CLIP help only when the frozen model already misclassifies the target domain, and proposes Competence-Gated Adaptation (CoGA), which measures CLIP's accuracy and margin on the support set to decide before training whether to intervene, achieving better and more stable source-free cross-domain few-shot learning.
